name: Checkmk
description: Checkmk monitoring: hosts and their configuration, live service states, acknowledged and unhandled problems, host groups and downtimes. REST API on your own site, bearer-style automation user auth.
instructions:
**Setup**
1. In Checkmk create an **automation user**: Setup → Users → Add user, tick *Automation secret for machine accounts*, and copy the secret. Give it the `guest` role for read-only access, or `admin` if you want the configuration endpoints.
2. Set `CHECKMK_URL` to your site root including the site name — `https://monitoring.example.com/mysite` — with no trailing slash. The site name is part of the path and leaving it out is the usual cause of a 404 that looks like a wrong version.
3. Set `CHECKMK_USERNAME` to the automation user and `CHECKMK_SECRET` to its secret.

**The Authorization header is `Bearer <user> <secret>`** — two space-separated values in one Bearer token, which is Checkmk's own scheme and looks wrong the first time you see it. The adapter assembles it.

**Setup vs Monitoring.** Checkmk's REST API has two halves and they answer different questions. `/domain-types/host_config/…` is the *configuration* — what has been set up. `/domain-types/host/…` and `/domain-types/service/…` are the *live monitoring state* — what is happening now. A question about a red service needs the second; a question about what is monitored needs the first.

**Live state is queried with a Livestatus expression.** The `query` parameter takes JSON like `{"op": "=", "left": "state", "right": "2"}` — state 0 is OK, 1 warning, 2 critical, 3 unknown. Combine with `{"op": "and", "expr": [...]}`.

**`columns` is repeated, not comma-separated.** Checkmk wants `columns=host_name&columns=state&columns=plugin_output`. The tools below send a useful default set.

**Changes need activation.** Anything written into the Setup half sits in a pending-changes queue until activated. This adapter is read-only, so it never leaves a half-applied change behind.

**Self-hosted, which is the thing to plan for.**
- On **AnythingMCP Cloud** the instance must be reachable from the public internet on a real hostname with a valid TLS certificate. A self-signed certificate will fail: the connector offers no trust-anything switch, and a homelab's default certificate is exactly the case that breaks.
- On an internal host (`monitoring.intern`, `10.0.0.x`), self-host AnythingMCP on the same network and add that host to `SSRF_ALLOWED_HOSTS`, or the outbound guard refuses the call before it is made.

tools.name: checkmk_get_version
tools.description: Read the Checkmk version and edition of this site. No parameters and the lightest permission — the fastest proof that URL, site name and automation secret all line up.

tools.name: checkmk_list_hosts
tools.description: List hosts from the *configuration*: what has been set up for monitoring, with folder, attributes and effective settings. Not the live state.

effective_attributes.description: When true, include attributes inherited from the folder.

search.description: Host name fragment to filter by.

tools.name: checkmk_get_host_config
tools.description: Read one host's configuration: its folder, IP address, tags, labels and the attributes it inherits.

hostName.description: Host name as configured in Checkmk.

tools.name: checkmk_list_host_states
tools.description: Read the *live* state of hosts: up, down or unreachable, with the check output and how long each has been that way.

query.description: Livestatus filter as JSON, e.g. {"op": "=", "left": "state", "right": "1"} for hosts that are down.

columns.description: One column name to include beyond the defaults.

tools.name: checkmk_list_service_states
tools.description: Read the *live* state of services — the red, amber and green checks. State 0 is OK, 1 warning, 2 critical, 3 unknown.

query.description: Livestatus filter as JSON, e.g. {"op": ">", "left": "state", "right": "0"} for everything not OK.

columns.description: One column name to include beyond the defaults.

tools.name: checkmk_list_host_services
tools.description: Read every service on one host with its current state and check output — the drill-down after a host has been flagged.

hostName.description: Host name as configured in Checkmk.

columns.description: One column name to include beyond the defaults.

tools.name: checkmk_list_host_groups
tools.description: List the host groups configured on this site with their alias, so a query can be scoped to a part of the estate.

tools.name: checkmk_list_downtimes
tools.description: List scheduled downtimes with their host, service, comment, author and window — the explanation for why an alert did not fire.

tools.name: checkmk_list_folders
tools.description: List the Checkmk folder tree with each folder's title, path and attributes — how hosts are organised and where settings are inherited from.

recursive.description: When true, return the whole tree rather than the top level.
